pr_title: fix(test runner): fixture teardown double error, testInfo.attach()
pr_body:
- Use file path, not content to calculate the attachment hash.
- Always cleanup fixture from the list on teardown, to avoid reporting
  teardown error multiple times: from the test, and from the cleanup.

Fixes #11341.

issue_context.title: [BUG] testInfo.attach(…) hangs with paths in fixtures
comments:
Test case added here: https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/11342/

Note: Looks like it is hanging on this line in `calculateFileSha1` : https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/359d523ec318106bf79d650b2b4458a1a388ebdf/packages/playwright-core/src/utils/utils.ts#L409

In writing the test, was also able to provide a fix. See https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/11342 for where it was actually fixed.

😄

review_comments: Can't have a bug in it if the code no longer exists! 😃
What's the reason for the switch to filename instead of contents? Regardless, filename hash seems much simpler (and I suppose negligibly faster depending on what was in the files).

Can you bring over the other test, too? 

https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/11342/files#diff-7baf8520adc91e87042c746455f6e8a73b78771e9ca03095c9b15437894a6b4aR107

I intentionally had two tests so I ensured the positive test case actually does work alongside the negative test case. (Afterall, the positive case is what lead us here 😀 so I'd want to know if we broke that in the future, and it feels different enough from the other attachment cases since it happens in fixture teardown as opposed to during the test.)
